pair.title: Pair a device
pair.sub: Compare a code so two computers trust each other — works even where discovery can't see them
pair.hostLead: On the other computer, open LanBeam → Pair → Join theirs, and enter these two:
pair.regenToast: New code — the old one, and any link you copied, no longer work
pair.noLan: No LAN address — connect to a network first
pair.linkLead: Or send them the pair link — it carries the address and the code, and opening it fills the form in
pair.joinLead: Open Pair in their LanBeam, then enter the address and pairing code it shows:
pair.joinPasteHint: Or just paste the pair link they sent you
pair.linkLoaded: Filled in from a pair link
pair.addrFrom: "{{name}}"'s address is filled in — you still need the code on their screen
pair.addrFromLink: Address filled in from a link — you still need the code on their screen
pair.addOnly: Just add the device, don't pair
pair.addOnlyHint: No code to compare and no trust — it simply shows up in your device list
pair.badAddr: Enter their address here, e.g. 192.168.1.8:51704 — or paste the pair link
pair.codeMixup: That looks like the pairing code — it goes on the right; this field is for their address
pair.rejected: They didn't accept that code — it's wrong or expired, or they're not on "Let them join me"
pair.unreachable: Can't reach {{addr}} — are both devices on the same network, and is LanBeam running there?
pair.identityMismatch: The device that answered isn't the one in the link — the link may be stale, or that address now belongs to another device
pair.busyPrefill: Already pairing — finish this one before opening another link
pair.foot: Once the verification codes match, both sides pin fingerprints — auto-recognized and auto-accepted on this network from then on
pair.compareBody: Your screen and "{{name}}"'s should now show the same digits
pair.compareWarn: They only match if nobody is relaying between you
pair.mismatchToast: Nothing was trusted. A mismatch can mean someone is relaying between you — try again on another network.
pair.unconfirmedToast: Verification codes never compared — nothing was trusted

share.title: Receive in a browser
share.copiedToast: Link copied · open it in a browser on the same network
share.lanNote: Local network only — the file goes straight from this device to theirs, never through a server. If a browser warns "not secure", that's normal for a local link; just continue.
share.stoppedToast: Sharing stopped · the link is dead
share.startFailed: Couldn't start sharing · check the files still exist, then reopen to try again
share.demoNote: Browser receive runs in the desktop app · this web demo has no local file server
share.foot: Local networks only · never leaves the LAN · the link dies when you stop sharing
share.liveSub: Files are being served on your LAN · click to manage
share.liveHint: Closing the share panel does NOT stop the share — the link keeps working until it expires, hits its download cap, or you press Stop. Click here to stop it.
share.keptToast: The link is still live — closing the panel doesn't stop a share. You can stop it from the sidebar.
share.adoptToast: Picked up the share that was already running

fp.warnTitle: "{{name}}" is answering with a different key
fp.warnSub: The new one is not trusted, and will not auto-accept
fp.explain: It may have reinstalled or reset its identity — or someone may be using the same name. The key IS the identity, so to LanBeam this is a brand-new device. To trust it, pair with it like one: pairing shows the same code on BOTH screens, and records trust only once a person says they match.
fp.removedToast: Old record deleted — the new device still has to be paired to be trusted
fp.foot: A key can't be "restored" — it can only be met again
